value: The Attorney-General is not a whole-time counsel for the Government
reasoning: The Attorney-General may speak in either House (Article 88), has a right of audience in all courts in India (Article 76(3)) and must be qualified to be a Supreme Court judge (Article 76(1)). He is not a full-time counsel or a government servant, and may take private practice that does not conflict with his duties, so D is the incorrect statement.

value: Statements 1 and 2 are correct; short notice questions are taken up after Question Hour, not during it
reasoning: A short notice question relates to a matter of urgent public importance and can be asked for oral answer on less than 10 days' notice, and it is admitted only if the Minister agrees to answer at short notice. In Lok Sabha practice it is answered immediately after Question Hour, so statement 3 is wrong. Runner-up is A (1, 2 and 3), which wins only if 'after Question Hour' is read as part of the Question Hour sitting.

value: The Tenth Schedule does not make the Supreme Court the final arbiter of unresolved cases
reasoning: The Tenth Schedule provides for disqualification on grounds of defection, exempts mergers (where two-thirds of the legislature party agree), and gives the decision to the Speaker or Chairman, whose decision it declares final. It contains no provision making the Supreme Court the final arbiter; courts review the presiding officer's decision only through judicial review (Kihoto Hollohan, 1992).

value: All three pairs are correctly matched
reasoning: Public health and sanitation is Entry 6 of the State List; citizenship, naturalisation and aliens is Entry 17 of the Union List; legal, medical and other professions is Entry 26 of the Concurrent List. All three pairs match.

value: Bacteria contain cytoplasm but viruses do not
reasoning: Bacteria are cells with cytoplasm and a cell membrane, while a virus is only nucleic acid in a protein coat, with no cytoplasm. Bacteria are prokaryotes and have no mitochondria, and viruses have neither mitochondria nor a cell membrane, so B, C and D are false.

value: The cell loses water (exosmosis in a hypertonic medium)
reasoning: When the surrounding medium is more concentrated (hypertonic), water moves out of the cell by osmosis from the region of higher water concentration, so the cell loses water and shrinks (plasmolysis in plant cells).
Rough ER is studded with ribosomes on its outer surface, which give it a rough, granular look under the electron microscope and make it the site of protein synthesis. Smooth ER lacks them.
Apical meristems at the tips of stems and roots add cells that increase length (primary growth). Lateral meristems increase girth, and intercalary meristems add length only at nodes or leaf bases.
The large central vacuole filled with cell sap presses the cytoplasm against the cell wall, giving turgor pressure that keeps plant cells turgid and rigid.
Pollen grains are formed in the pollen sacs of the anther, the top part of the stamen. Style and stigma belong to the pistil, and the corolla is the petals.

value: The marginal product of the variable factor diminishes
reasoning: The Law of Diminishing Returns (variable proportions) states that adding more units of a variable input to a fixed input eventually makes the marginal product of the variable input fall. It is a statement about physical product, not revenue.

value: The monopoly MR curve lies below, not above, its AR curve
reasoning: A monopolist faces a downward sloping demand (AR) curve, so to sell an extra unit it must cut the price on all units, which puts MR below AR. The other statements are true: a competitive firm's AR = MR is horizontal, long-run competitive profits are normal, and a monopolist can be in equilibrium with rising, falling or constant MC.

value: Quantity demanded does not change at all whatever the price change (perfectly inelastic)
reasoning: Zero price elasticity means the percentage change in quantity is zero for any percentage change in price, so the demand curve is vertical. Options B and D describe inelastic but non-zero elasticity, and C describes elastic demand.

Using the midpoint method: change in quantity 80 divided by average quantity 200 is 0.4, and change in price 20 divided by average price 100 is 0.2, so elasticity is 0.4/0.2 = 2.0. The simple point formula from the initial values gives (80/240)/(20/90) = 1.5, which is not offered, so the question intends the arc method.
By the Fisher approximation, real interest rate = nominal rate minus inflation = 24% - 10% = 14%. (The exact formula 1.24/1.10 - 1 gives about 12.7%, which is closest to 14% among the options.)
Methanol (CH3OH) was originally obtained by the destructive distillation of wood, hence the name wood spirit (wood alcohol). Ethanol is grain spirit.

value: Lime juice (a true solution) does not show the Tyndall effect
reasoning: The Tyndall effect is the scattering of a light beam by particles of colloidal or larger size. Milk in water and starch solution are colloids, and freshly mixed chalk in water is a suspension whose large particles also scatter light, while lime juice is treated as a true solution whose dissolved particles are too small to scatter. Runner-up is A, which would win only if suspensions were held not to show the effect.

Raising pressure pushes gas molecules closer together and lowering temperature reduces their kinetic energy, so intermolecular attraction can hold them as a liquid. A gas must also be below its critical temperature to liquefy.

Bauxite is the main ore of aluminium, magnetite (Fe3O4) is an iron ore, malachite (basic copper carbonate) is a copper ore and calamine (ZnCO3) is a zinc ore. Only A lists them in the order Al, Fe, Cu, Zn.

value: Ascorbic acid (vitamin C) has no COOH group
reasoning: Citric, lactic and tartaric acids are carboxylic acids with COOH groups. Ascorbic acid is a cyclic lactone whose acidity comes from an enol OH group, so it contains no free COOH group.

value: Sulphuric acid and sodium hydrogencarbonate solution
reasoning: In a soda-acid extinguisher, sulphuric acid mixes with sodium hydrogencarbonate (baking soda) solution to produce carbon dioxide, which forces out the water and smothers the fire.

The Kakori train robbery (1925) was carried out by the Hindustan Republican Association, and Ram Prasad Bismil, Rajendra Lahiri and Ashfaqulla Khan were hanged in the case. Surya Sen led the Chittagong Armoury Raid (1930) and had no part in Kakori.

Bhagat Singh was strongly influenced by socialist and Marxist ideas, and he was a leading member of the Hindustan Socialist Republican Association, so 1 and 2 are true. The 1929 Assembly bombs were deliberately thrown where no one would be hurt, 'to make the deaf hear', so statement 3 is false.

Vidyasagar shaped modern Bengali prose (1 true) and was a strong champion of girls' education (3 true). He received the title 'Vidyasagar' from Sanskrit College, Calcutta, not Presidency College (2 false), and he argued for widow remarriage precisely by citing scriptural support, notably the Parashara Samhita (4 false).
On 13 April 1919 troops under Brigadier-General Reginald Dyer fired on an unarmed crowd in Jallianwala Bagh, Amritsar, without giving any warning to disperse. All three statements hold.
The Election Commission first used EVMs with VVPAT in the by-election to the Noksen Assembly constituency of Nagaland in September 2013. North Paravur, Kerala was where EVMs were first used, in 1982.

value: Unfinished business: the pursuit of rights and choices for all
reasoning: UNFPA's State of World Population 2019 report, marking 25 years since the Cairo ICPD, was titled 'Unfinished business: the pursuit of rights and choices for all'. 'Worlds apart' was 2017, 'The power of choice' was 2018 and the 'girl at this decisive age' report was 2016.
The Saraswati Samman for 2018 went to Telugu poet K. Siva Reddy for his collection 'Pakkaki Ottigilite'. Mahabaleshwar Sail won for 2016, Sitanshu Yashaschandra for 2017 and Padma Sachdev for 2015.
Kandhamal Haldi is grown mainly by tribal farmers in Kandhamal district of southern Odisha and received its GI tag in 2019.
The Order of Zayed (Zayed Medal), named after Sheikh Zayed bin Sultan Al Nahyan, is the UAE's highest civilian honour; it was conferred on Prime Minister Narendra Modi in 2019.

In any mechanical wave, including a longitudinal one, the particles of the medium only oscillate about their mean positions while the disturbance and its energy travel onward. No material is carried along.
Uranium has atomic number 92, so U-235 has 92 protons and 235 - 92 = 143 neutrons.
Power = force x velocity, so F = P/v = 3000 W / 5 m/s = 600 N.

value: An electromagnetic wave is transverse, not longitudinal
reasoning: In an EM wave the electric and magnetic fields oscillate perpendicular to each other and to the direction of travel, so it is transverse; that is also why it can be polarized. EM waves carry energy and momentum and can be reflected.
Sound is a mechanical, longitudinal wave that needs a material medium. Light, radio waves and microwaves are all parts of the electromagnetic spectrum.

Diamond has a very high refractive index (about 2.42) and hence a small critical angle (about 24 degrees), so light entering a cut diamond is totally internally reflected many times before leaving, which makes it sparkle.

value: Statements 2 and 3: a frost-free period of about 100 days and light clay or heavy loam soil
reasoning: Wheat is a cool-season crop: it needs moderate temperatures of roughly 10-25 degrees C while growing, so an optimum of around 30 degrees C is wrong. Standard geography texts state that it needs a frost-free growing season of about 100 days and grows best on light clay or heavy loam soils. Runner-up is A, which would win only if 30 degrees C were taken as acceptable for the ripening stage.
Gwadar is a deep-sea port on the Arabian Sea coast of Balochistan, Pakistan, developed with Chinese investment under the China-Pakistan Economic Corridor. Iran's comparable port nearby is Chabahar.

value: The end of the Cretaceous period (Deccan Traps)
reasoning: The Deccan Traps, the huge basalt flows covering the north-west of the peninsula, erupted through fissures at the end of the Cretaceous period, around 66 million years ago.

Factor out 3^9: the sum is 3^9 (1 + 27 + 729 + 3^(n-9)) = 3^9 (757 + 3^(n-9)). Since 3^9 = (3^3)^3 is already a cube, we need 757 + 3^(n-9) to be a cube; n = 14 gives 757 + 243 = 1000 = 10^3. The other choices give 760, 766 and 838, none of which is a cube.

value: The circle has the greater area
reasoning: With perimeter P, the square's area is P^2/16 and the circle's is P^2/(4 pi), about P^2/12.57, which is larger. Among all shapes with a given perimeter the circle encloses the most area.

The conditions say (x, y) and (u, v) are perpendicular unit vectors, so the matrix with rows (x, y) and (u, v) is orthogonal and its columns are also orthonormal: x^2 + u^2 = 1, y^2 + v^2 = 1 and xy + uv = 0. For example, x = cos t, y = sin t, u = -sin t, v = cos t satisfies all three.
A non-leap year has 365 days = 52 weeks + 1 day, so day 365 is 364 days (exactly 52 weeks) after day 1 and falls on the same weekday. If 1 January is a Sunday, 31 December is also a Sunday.

Take the start as (0, 0) facing north: 10 m forward reaches (0, 10), turning right and walking 10 m reaches (10, 10) facing east. Turning left he walks 5 m north to (10, 15), left again 15 m west to (-5, 15), and left again 15 m south to (-5, 0). He is 5 m from the start.

value: Participation of workers in the management of local self-government is not a Directive Principle
reasoning: Article 41 (right to work, education and public assistance), Article 44 (Uniform Civil Code) and Article 50 (separation of judiciary from executive) are all Directive Principles. Article 43A provides for workers' participation in the management of industries, not of local self-government, so D is not provided for.

Under the Mountbatten Plan, the members of the Punjab and Bengal Legislative Assemblies were to meet in two groups (Muslim-majority and other districts), and if either group voted for partition the province would be divided. The Cripps proposals and the Nehru Report had no such procedure, and the Beveridge Report is a British welfare document.

value: Only statement 2: bureaucracy has structural and behavioural characteristics
reasoning: Weber's ideal type describes bureaucracy as a rational-legal organisation marked by structural features (hierarchy, division of labour, written rules) and behavioural features (impersonality, rationality, rule-orientation), so statement 2 is correct. Viewing bureaucracy in terms of dominant class character is the Marxist critique, not Weber's ideal type, so 1 is wrong. Runner-up is D, which would win only if the setter regarded 'behavioural' as alien to Weber's purely structural model.

value: DPSP do not take precedence over Fundamental Rights in a conflict
reasoning: Directive Principles are non-justiciable (Article 37) yet fundamental in governance, and the State must apply them in making laws and administering. In a conflict, Fundamental Rights, which are enforceable, generally prevail (State of Madras v. Champakam Dorairajan, 1951), with only limited exceptions such as Article 31C, so C is incorrect.

value: Statements 1 and 2: constitutional government and guaranteed civil liberties
reasoning: Liberal democracy rests on constitutional government under formal legal rules and on guarantees of civil liberties and individual rights. Its essence is limited government, so investing political authority with potentially unlimited power (statement 3) is the opposite of a liberal-democratic feature.

Phreatophytes are deep-rooted plants, such as mesquite and some acacias, that draw water from the water table, which lets them survive in arid and semi-arid regions. Plants of moist shade are sciophytes and plants of rocks are lithophytes.
Hydra and sea anemone are cnidarians with cnidoblasts (stinging cells). Planaria and liver fluke are flatworms, sea urchin and sea cucumber are echinoderms, and Euplectella and Sycon are sponges.

Phototropism is directional growth in response to light; a shoot growing towards the light source shows positive phototropism (roots usually show negative phototropism). Photonasty is a non-directional movement and photoperiodism is a response to day length.
Root hairs are tubular outgrowths of root epidermal cells that greatly increase the surface area for absorbing water and minerals. Endodermis is an inner tissue layer and stomata occur on leaves.
Quartz is crystalline silicon dioxide, SiO2, so the element it contains is silicon. Its piezoelectric property is why quartz crystals are used in watches and oscillators.

Sodium hexametaphosphate (Calgon) softens water by forming soluble complexes with Ca2+ and Mg2+ ions, and is the standard textbook answer for the Calgon process. Mg(HCO3)2 is itself a cause of temporary hardness. Runner-up is B: trisodium phosphate also softens water by precipitating calcium and magnesium phosphates, so B would win if the setter had that use in mind.
Na2X means the anion has charge -2 (X2-), since each sodium is +1. Aluminium is Al3+, so balancing charges needs 2 Al3+ (total +6) and 3 X2- (total -6), giving Al2X3.
In a closed economy without taxes the multiplier is 1/(1 - MPC) = 1/(1 - 0.9) = 1/0.1 = 10.

value: Positive (equal to the MPC, between 0 and 1)
reasoning: In Keynes's consumption function, consumption rises as income rises, but by less than the rise in income, so the slope (the marginal propensity to consume) is positive and less than one.

value: The (maximum retail) price printed on biscuit packets
reasoning: A price ceiling is a legal maximum above which a good cannot be sold, and the MRP printed on a packet is exactly such an upper limit on the selling price. Minimum support prices and minimum wages are price floors, and airline fares in India are set by the market. Runner-up is A, which would win only if airfares were taken to be capped by regulation.

value: The economy must give up some of one good to produce more of another
reasoning: On the production possibility frontier all resources are fully and efficiently used, so producing more of one good requires producing less of the other (opportunity cost). The PPF is downward sloping, and resources are limited, so B, C and D are false.

The paradox of thrift, that a general attempt to save more can lower aggregate income and so fail to raise total saving, was popularised by Keynes in the General Theory (1936). The idea had earlier roots, for example in Mandeville, but it is associated with Keynes.
The Indian Forest Act of 1878 classified forests into reserved, protected and village forests. The 1865 Act was the first Forest Act and did not make this three-way division.

value: Brahmo Samaj (1828), Paramhansa Mandali (1849), Arya Samaj (1875), Ramakrishna Mission (1897)
reasoning: Raja Ram Mohan Roy founded the Brahmo Samaj in 1828, the Paramhansa Mandali was set up in Bombay in 1849, Dayananda Saraswati founded the Arya Samaj in 1875, and Vivekananda founded the Ramakrishna Mission in 1897. The order is 3, 4, 2, 1.
